subject: Hosted inference cost outline & supported models
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@citrine-labs.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted inference cost outline & supported models

Hi Tessa,

We're evaluating hosted inference providers for a customer-facing feature (real-time summarization + search). Can you send a high-level cost outline per 1M tokens (input vs output) for your hosted API, plus the short list of supported models and any guidance on which models are appropriate for low-latency production use?

A couple quick notes about our workload: ~75% of calls are short prompts (~50 tokens input, ~150 tokens output), and the rest are longer (up to ~2k output). We expect to start at ~5M tokens/month and grow to ~200M over 6–9 months.

Also, if you have a one-page PDF or spreadsheet we can share with engineering, that'd be great.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Product
Citrine Labs
samir@citrine-labs.com
+1 (415) 555-0172

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@citrine-labs.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted inference cost outline & supported models

Samir —

Thanks for the context. Attaching a short "Hosted IO Cost Outline" that summarizes baseline per-1M token IO rates and a recommended model roster. Quick summary below to unblock you immediately:

- Baseline hosted IO (per 1M tokens):
  - Input tokens: $0.90 per 1M tokens
  - Output tokens: $1.80 per 1M tokens

- Model tiers (common picks for production):
  - Cost-optimized / low latency: redwood-3b, psi-7b (recommended for short prompts and tight SLOs)
  - Balanced quality/latency: redwood-13b, cedar-13b
  - High-quality / larger context: redwood-65b (use for long-form generation or higher quality checks)

Notes:
- The baseline above is for our standard hosted single-tenant model instances. We recommend redwood-3b or psi-7b for your 50-token prompt / 150-token response profile to keep latency low and unit cost favorable.
- We can enable automatic prefix KV caching and request-level batching which generally reduces effective per-token cost for repeated prompts.

I've attached the one-pager (PDF) and a short model-compatibility table. If you want volume-tier pricing or a committed discount path, I can loop in Ben Carter to propose a brief tiered pricing schedule and commit options.

Attachments: citrine-hosted-cost-outline-20280620.pdf (1 page)

Best,

Tessa Morgan

Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir@citrine-labs.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jun 2028 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted inference cost outline & supported models

Tessa —

Thanks, that helps a lot. A couple follow-ups:

1) Can you confirm whether the per-1M token numbers include any request/response rounding rules (e.g., how you count tokens for streaming responses)? We need to make sure our cost model matches actual billing.
2) For the redwood-3b option, what typical p95 latency do you see at the single-request level (no batching) for a 50-in / 150-out prompt in your hosted environment?
3) For committed discounts, we're likely to be able to commit to a 3–6 month pilot with a ~50M token minimum. What discount bands apply at that scale?

Also, can Ben provide a simple committed pricing example (showing effective per-1M rates at 50M and 200M/month)?

—Samir

Samir — looping in Ben (CC) to give a committed discount example and formal tiered options. See quick illustrative bands below (we'll produce a short spreadsheet if you want to share with finance):

- Example committed tiers (hosted IO, effective per 1M tokens):
  - 0–10M / month: input $0.90 | output $1.80 (baseline)
  - 10–50M / month: input $0.72 | output $1.44 (20% discount)
  - 50–200M / month: input $0.54 | output $1.08 (40% discount)
  - 200M+ / month: custom enterprise pricing (volume + SLA)

Ben — can you confirm these bands and provide p95 latency numbers for redwood-3b at single-request SLOs (50/150 tokens) in hosted mode? Also attaching the one-pager for reference.

Next steps for Citrine: if the 50M pilot looks reasonable, let's do a 3-month pilot with the 20–40% preliminary commitment band and an engineering jumpstart (1 day onboarding + sample prompts eval). If you want, we can put together a short mutual action plan.

Thanks,
Tessa
